subject: mathematics
question_text: Prove that cos²(π/8) + cos²(3π/8) + cos²(5π/8) + cos²(7π/8) = 2.

verification.note: Source: Baby Bullet-Q, Junior Inter Maths-1A (Sri Publishers, Machilipatnam), book p.109 — from the book's separate "STAR QUESTIONS PLUS" bank, answer 174. That bank (book pp.98-111, answers 142-180) sits AFTER all the numbered chapters and is organised by chapter rather than forming part of any chapter's own inventory; it is authored into this unit because that is where the question belongs on the paper (founder decision 2026-08-22). SECTION: classed SAQ on its length and shape. The bank prints no mark cut, so this classification is OURS. Printed appearances: none — this answer carries no year tag. The same closing move as the previous question, but each of the three larger angles needs its OWN rewriting — one as π/2 − θ, one as π/2 + θ, one as π − θ. ⚠ THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S — the bank prints no [N Marks] tags anywhere. The shapes used follow the splits the book DOES print elsewhere: 1+1 for a 2-mark VSAQ (answers 100, 101 on book p.82), 1+1+1+1 or 1+2+1 for a 4-mark SAQ (answers 58, 59 on p.63 and 61 on p.64), and the granular split for a 7-mark LAQ (answer 32 on p.44). This is a coaching publication, not a TSBIE document, so the split stays unverified until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

recall_prompt: Say how you would do this one — name each move in order.

steps.label: Rewrite 3π/8
steps.margin_note: First mark. 3π/8 = (4π − π)/8 = π/2 − π/8, and cos(π/2 − θ) = sin θ.

recall.must_convey: That 3π/8 = π/2 − π/8, so cos(3π/8) = sin(π/8).
accept: three pi by eight is pi by two minus pi by eight so its cosine is sine of pi by eight
the first large angle becomes a sine
cos of pi by two minus theta is sin theta
three pi by eight ante pi by two minus pi by eight

steps.why: Writing 4π/8 as the common numerator makes the complement visible. All three rewritings in this question use the same trick.
common_mistakes: Leaving 3π/8 alone and looking for its value.

steps.label: Rewrite 5π/8 and 7π/8
steps.margin_note: Half the marks, and the two to watch — 5π/8 goes to π/2 PLUS π/8 (giving −sin), and 7π/8 goes to π MINUS π/8 (giving −cos).

accept: five pi by eight is pi by two plus pi by eight giving minus sine, and seven pi by eight is pi minus pi by eight giving minus cosine
one becomes minus sine and the other minus cosine
the two shifts are different, one is pi by two plus and one is pi minus
five pi by eight lo plus, seven pi by eight lo pi minus

steps.why: These three angles do NOT all shift the same way. Using π/2 − θ for all of them is the common error, and it breaks the pairing.
common_mistakes: Applying π/2 − θ to all three angles.

steps.label: Square and pair
steps.margin_note: Last mark. Squaring removes both minus signs, and the four terms fall into two Pythagorean pairs.

recall.must_convey: That squaring removes the minus signs and the four terms pair into two Pythagorean identities, giving 2.
accept: squaring removes the minus signs and the four terms pair up as cos squared plus sin squared twice giving two
each pair is one so the total is two
square cheste minus poddi, rendu pairs one one, total two

steps.why: Every term ends up as a square of sin(π/8) or cos(π/8) — two of each. The value of π/8 itself is never needed.
